items.title: Nvidia board launches independent inquiry; shares under premarket pressure
items.summary: Nvidia confirmed an independent board inquiry into reports CEO Jensen Huang was targeted by a foreign intelligence effort. The board said it has no reason to believe secrets or national security were compromised. Early premarket accounts indicate NVDA down roughly 4–6%, adding governance uncertainty to an already weak semiconductor tape; no operating impairment has been established.

observations.value: Independent inquiry announced November 8; no evidence of compromised corporate secrets identified by board

observations.label: Fundamental impact
observations.value: No confirmed change to chip production, demand, guidance or financial results

items.key_finding: Board-confirmed governance investigation produces significant premarket repricing, but operational damage remains unverified.

items.title: Brent and WTI decline on Iran de-escalation talk despite serious Hormuz security warnings
items.summary: Reuters reported Brent down 1.7% to $96.67 and WTI down 1.0% to $89.87 at 08:30 GMT as U.S. comments lowered expectations of renewed Iran strikes. UKMTO's November 8 notices document tanker security incidents, but no new physical oil-volume loss was established. Last week's approximately 16% Brent decline underscores the market's de-escalation pricing despite unresolved maritime risk.

items.title: Houthi missile attack damages Aramco administration building in Riyadh
items.summary: Saudi Arabia says it intercepted ballistic and cruise missiles early Sunday, but falling debris damaged an Aramco office building in Riyadh; the Houthis claimed the attack. Saudi officials reported no casualties, and no refinery, pipeline or crude-production outage has been established. This widens regional infrastructure risk alongside Hormuz shipping attacks, but does not yet demonstrate an additional physical oil-supply loss.

items.title: Anthropic reportedly secures $3.4 billion of gas-fired generation commitments for AI data centers
items.summary: The Financial Times reports Anthropic took over commitments for 1.7 GW of Caterpillar gas-fired generators originally ordered by OnePWR, in a deal agreed in late September and disclosed November 8. Reuters independently reported the FT account but said it could not verify it. This is a significant power-supply bottleneck signal, not evidence of a new Caterpillar equipment order.

items.title: Separate outbound tanker reportedly struck by unknown projectile in Strait of Hormuz
items.summary: UKMTO Warning 200-26, reported November 8, describes a tanker struck by an unknown projectile while sailing outbound through the Strait of Hormuz on November 7. The company security officer reported that the crew were safe and no environmental impact was known. This is distinct from the Khasab tanker fire and Gulf of Oman bulker strike already in the feed; the attacker and incremental oil-flow impact remain unverified.
